records.headline: The Evening Star prints an item: W. S. McGunness of Washington
records.summary_en: The Evening Star prints an item: W. S. McGunness of Washington was to be the first witness at this afternoon's hearing of the inquiry by Phelan of California into the conduct of James M. Sullivan, minister to the Dominican Republic. McGunness, who has been active in politics, was expected to tell what he knew of the efforts made in Washington by financiers interested in Santo Domingo to have Sullivan appointed, and the appointment confirmed by the Senate. At yesterday's session Walker W. Vick, former receiver general of Dominican customs and instigator of the present investigation, testified: 'One man told me that he had been promised a postmastership if he would 'get me.'' He intimated that Joseph P. Tumulty, secretary to the President, had been responsible for Secretary Bryan's attitude toward him. This had grown out of rivalry between them for Tumulty's present post, he thought. Earl Harding, a newspaperman, who has been investigating Sullivan in behalf of his paper, testified that he had been told that Tumulty had said that 'the White House regarded Vick as a sore-head and that he would have been removed from his position had he not resigned.' Joseph P. Tumulty, secretary to President Wilson, issued a statement today referring to testimony given yesterday by Walker W. Vick, saying he was ready to testify before Mr. Phelan at any time, either here or in New York.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star publica una nota: W. S. McGunness, de Washington, sería el primer testigo en la audiencia de esta tarde de la investigación de Phelan de California sobre la conducta de James M. Sullivan, ministro en la República Dominicana. Se esperaba que McGunness, que ha sido activo en la política, dijera lo que sabía de los esfuerzos hechos en Washington por financieros interesados en Santo Domingo para que Sullivan fuera nombrado, y el nombramiento confirmado por el Senado. En la sesión de ayer, Walker W. Vick, anteriormente recaudador general de las aduanas dominicanas e instigador de la presente investigación, declaró: «Un hombre me dijo que se le había prometido un puesto de administrador de correos si acababa conmigo». Dio a entender que Joseph P. Tumulty, secretario del Presidente, había sido responsable de la actitud del secretario Bryan hacia él. Esto había surgido de la rivalidad entre ellos por el puesto actual de Tumulty, pensaba. Earl Harding, un periodista, que ha estado investigando a Sullivan en nombre de su periódico, declaró que se le había dicho que Tumulty había dicho que «la Casa Blanca consideraba a Vick un resentido y que habría sido removido de su puesto si no hubiera renunciado». Joseph P. Tumulty, secretario del presidente Wilson, emitió hoy una declaración en referencia al testimonio dado ayer por Walker W. Vick, diciendo que estaba listo para declarar ante el Sr. Phelan en cualquier momento, ya fuera aquí o en Nueva York.

records.headline: The Washington Herald prints an item: William S. McGinnis testified
records.summary_en: The Washington Herald prints an item: William S. McGinnis testified today before Commissioner Phelan, who is investigating charges against James Mark Sullivan, United States Minister to the Dominican republic, that Beer had captured the finances of Santo Domingo, and was planning to put its officers into Nicaragua. Sullivan was appointed by the efforts of Beer, McGinnis said, and he called him the 'big chief.' When the two met in a Washington hotel, after Sullivan's appointment as Minister, the latter told him: 'Things are going fine, Bill. The big chief will soon be not only financial agent of Santo Domingo, but of Nicaragua as well.' When McGinnis repeated the conversation to Beer, the 'big chief' said, 'for God's sake, keep quiet about that.' On another occasion Beer told him in Washington, 'This Santo Domingo deal has been the dream of my life. There's millions in it. I've been waiting for it for years.' Representative James A. Hamill, of New Jersey, according to the witness, said: 'Beer gets me so worked up over Nicaragua that every morning I wake up thinking I'm going to get $999,000.' McGinnis, formerly assistant superintendent of the railway mail service, told in detail the final steps to put Sullivan into office, even after Secretary Tumulty had told Representative Hamill that the White House heard Beer was interested in the Banco Nacionale of Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald publica una nota: William S. McGinnis declaró hoy ante el comisionado Phelan, que investiga las acusaciones contra James Mark Sullivan, ministro de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana, que Beer había capturado las finanzas de Santo Domingo, y planeaba poner a sus oficiales en Nicaragua. Sullivan fue nombrado por los esfuerzos de Beer, dijo McGinnis, y lo llamó el «gran jefe». Cuando los dos se encontraron en un hotel de Washington, después del nombramiento de Sullivan como ministro, este le dijo: «Las cosas van bien, Bill. El gran jefe pronto será no solo el agente financiero de Santo Domingo, sino también de Nicaragua». Cuando McGinnis repitió la conversación a Beer, el «gran jefe» dijo: «Por el amor de Dios, no hables de eso». En otra ocasión Beer le dijo en Washington: «Este negocio de Santo Domingo ha sido el sueño de mi vida. Hay millones en él. He estado esperándolo por años». El representante James A. Hamill, de Nueva Jersey, según el testigo, dijo: «Beer me altera tanto con lo de Nicaragua que cada mañana me despierto pensando que voy a recibir $999,000». McGinnis, anteriormente superintendente asistente del servicio de correo ferroviario, contó en detalle los pasos finales para poner a Sullivan en el cargo, incluso después de que el secretario Tumulty había dicho al representante Hamill que la Casa Blanca había oído que Beer estaba interesado en el Banco Nacionale de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Wheeling Intelligencer prints an item: New York, Jan. 19
records.summary_en: The Wheeling Intelligencer prints an item: New York, Jan. 19. Alleged political activities of Congressman James A. Hamill, of New Jersey, W. Beer of New York, and John O. Gray, of Wilmington, Del., in procuring the appointment of James M. Sullivan as minister to the Dominican republic were described today at the investigation which is being conducted by Senator-elect Phelan, of California, into Sullivan's fitness to hold office. W. G. McGunness, of Washington, who described himself as a personal friend of President McKinley and a 'Republican politician,' testified that Beer and Sullivan had promised him the position of director of posts in Santo Domingo in return for his assistance in promoting Sullivan's candidacy. The position was to be a 'sinecure,' said the witness. He described meetings which he said were held between Beer, Hamill and Sullivan in Washington, previous to Sullivan's appointment, the subject of which was ways and means to get the ear of Secretary Bryan. Beer, it has been brought out in previous testimony, was attorney for the Banco Nacional interests, Santo Domingo, who are charged with schemes to exploit public works contracts with the aid of Sullivan.
records.summary_es: The Wheeling Intelligencer publica una nota: W. G. McGunness, de Washington, declaró que Beer y Sullivan le habían prometido el puesto de director de correos en Santo Domingo a cambio de su ayuda para promover la candidatura de Sullivan. El puesto iba a ser una «sinecura», dijo el testigo. Se describió a sí mismo como amigo personal del presidente McKinley y un «político republicano». Las supuestas actividades políticas del congresista James A. Hamill, de Nueva Jersey, W. Beer de Nueva York, y John O. Gray, de Wilmington, Delaware, para procurar el nombramiento de James M. Sullivan como ministro en la República Dominicana fueron descritas hoy en la investigación que conduce el senador electo Phelan, de California, sobre la aptitud de Sullivan para ocupar el cargo. Describió reuniones que dijo se celebraron entre Beer, Hamill y Sullivan en Washington, antes del nombramiento de Sullivan, cuyo tema fue los medios para ganarse el oído del secretario Bryan. Beer, se ha revelado en testimonios anteriores, era abogado de los intereses del Banco Nacional de Santo Domingo, a quienes se acusa de maquinaciones para explotar contratos de obras públicas con la ayuda de Sullivan. Nueva York, 19 de enero.

records.headline: Beers Intended to Divide Swag
records.summary_en: The Fergus County Democrat prints an item: M. K. Davis of New York, a contractor for supplies, testified he had been informed by Beers, while the two were on their way to Santo Domingo, Davis with the expectation of securing government contracts, which, he said, Beers had represented to him were to be had. The witness said that at the same time he had taken Beers' statement seriously, but when Senator-elect James Phelan, who is conducting the inquiry, and his attorney, Charles H. Strong, expressed surprise that he had so regarded it, Davis asserted he now believed the statement to be 'silly rot.' He declared Beers evidently was trying to make an impression and 'using all means in his power to get money.' That Minister Sullivan had encouraged the Dominican government to bombard the city of Puerto Plata during a revolution in October, 1913, in spite of the fact that it would endanger American property there, was charged in testimony by G. O. Baker, a construction engineer. Baker had a contract for building a power house in that city for a Boston concern and said he protested to Minister Sullivan, asking intervention against a threatened attack on the city by a Dominican gunboat patrolling the river. The city was at that time in the possession of revolutionists, and although it was defended by a so-called fort, Baker said it was in no sense fortified, as the entire artillery of the fort consisted of one powder gun.
records.summary_es: The Fergus County Democrat publica: M. K. Davis, de Nueva York, un contratista de suministros, declaró que había sido informado por Beers, mientras los dos iban en camino a Santo Domingo, Davis con la expectativa de conseguir contratos del gobierno, que, dijo, Beers le había representado que podían obtenerse. El testigo dijo que en ese momento había tomado en serio la declaración de Beers, pero cuando el senador electo James Phelan, que conduce la investigación, y su abogado, Charles H. Strong, expresaron sorpresa de que la hubiera considerado así, Davis afirmó que ahora creía que la declaración era una «tontería absurda». Declaró que Beers evidentemente trataba de causar una impresión y de «usar todos los medios en su poder para conseguir dinero». Que el ministro Sullivan había alentado al gobierno dominicano a bombardear la ciudad de Puerto Plata durante una revolución en octubre de 1913, a pesar de que ello pondría en peligro la propiedad americana allí, fue denunciado en el testimonio de G. O. Baker, un ingeniero de construcción. Baker tenía un contrato para construir una planta eléctrica en esa ciudad para una empresa de Boston y dijo que protestó ante el ministro Sullivan, pidiendo intervención contra un amenazado ataque a la ciudad por una cañonera dominicana que patrullaba el río. La ciudad estaba en ese momento en posesión de los revolucionarios, y aunque estaba defendida por un llamado fuerte, Baker dijo que no estaba fortificada en ningún sentido, ya que toda la artillería del fuerte consistía en un cañón de pólvora.

records.headline: Glynn Makes Denial
records.summary_en: The Fergus County Democrat prints an item: Former Governor Martin H. Glynn issued a statement tonight calling the statement of M. E. Davis in the Sullivan investigation an absolute falsehood. Albany, N. Y., Jan. 20. 'The statement of M. E. Davis in the investigation of James M. Sullivan, the American minister to the Dominican republic, that I am interested in Santo Domingo matters is an absolute falsehood,' said former Governor Martin H. Glynn. 'I do not know Mr. Davis and never heard of him before. I do not know Mr. Sullivan and have no interest whatever in his doings. I am not interested in Santo Domingo; never was and never hope to be. I know nothing about the matter and cannot understand why my name has been dragged into it. I have been acquainted with William G. Beers for years, but I am not interested with him in any enterprise.'
records.summary_es: The Fergus County Democrat publica una nota: Martin H. Glynn, exgobernador, emitió esta noche una declaración en la que calificó de falsedad absoluta la declaración de M. E. Davis en la investigación de Sullivan. Albany, N. Y., 20 de enero. «La declaración de M. E. Davis en la investigación de James M. Sullivan, el ministro americano en la República Dominicana, de que estoy interesado en los asuntos de Santo Domingo es una falsedad absoluta», dijo el exgobernador Martin H. Glynn. «No conozco al Sr. Davis y nunca había oído hablar de él. No conozco al Sr. Sullivan y no tengo ningún interés en sus asuntos. No estoy interesado en Santo Domingo; nunca lo estuve y nunca espero estarlo. No sé nada del asunto y no puedo entender por qué mi nombre ha sido arrastrado a esto. He conocido a William G. Beers por años, pero no estoy interesado con él en ninguna empresa».

records.headline: JACK ROSE SOUGHT IN SULLIVAN PROBE American Minister Charged With Fostering Puerta Plata Bombardment.
records.summary_en: The New Britain Herald prints an item: Commissioner Phelan announced that ex-Governor Glynn of New York and ex-Governor J. Franklin Fort of New Jersey had been asked to appear. It was reported that Desidario Arias, revolutionist leader, had recommended that it would 'be a good thing to shoot off three or four good Americans' in order to bring about American intervention. Mr. Glynn was recently mentioned in testimony as having given Beer a letter of introduction to Secretary Bryan. Mr. Fort went to Santo Domingo recently to investigate affairs there for this government. Commissioner Phelan is also trying to procure the attendance of Jack Rose, one of the witnesses at the trial of Police Lieutenant Becker for the murder of Herman Rosenthal. Sullivan acted as Rose's counsel in the case and was associated with him, according to testimony in the present investigation, in the promotion of prizefights in Waterbury, Conn. Albany, N. Y., Jan. 21. 'The statement of M. E. Davis in the investigation of James M. Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican republic, that I am interested in Santo Domingo matters, is an absolute falsehood,' said ex-Governor Martin H. Glynn.
records.summary_es: The New Britain Herald publica una nota: El comisionado Phelan anunció que se había pedido que comparecieran el exgobernador Glynn de Nueva York y el exgobernador J. Franklin Fort de Nueva Jersey. Se informó que Desidario Arias, líder revolucionario, había recomendado que «sería bueno matar a tiros a tres o cuatro buenos americanos» para provocar la intervención americana. El Sr. Glynn fue mencionado recientemente en testimonios como quien había dado a Beer una carta de presentación para el secretario Bryan. El Sr. Fort fue a Santo Domingo recientemente para investigar los asuntos allí para este gobierno. El comisionado Phelan también trata de procurar la asistencia de Jack Rose, uno de los testigos en el juicio del teniente de policía Becker por el asesinato de Herman Rosenthal. Sullivan actuó como abogado de Rose en el caso y estuvo asociado con él, según testimonios en la presente investigación, en la promoción de peleas de boxeo en Waterbury, Connecticut. Albany, N. Y., 21 de enero. «La declaración de M. E. Davis en la investigación de James M. Sullivan, ministro americano en la República Dominicana, de que estoy interesado en los asuntos de Santo Domingo, es una falsedad absoluta», dijo el exgobernador Martin H. Glynn.

records.headline: DECLARES SULLIVAN WAS TO SHARE GRAFT Bryan Knew of Alleged Conspiracy of Dominican Minister, Says Witness.
records.summary_en: The Pierre Weekly Free Press prints an item: Testimony that Secretary of State Bryan was informed that James M. Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican republic, figured in an alleged conspiracy to exploit public contracts in that republic, was heard today at the inquiry by Senator-elect Phelan into the minister's fitness. James L. Bryne, of Boston, a construction engineer, testified that he had told Mr. Bryan that the minister's cousin, Timothy J. Sullivan, had told him that the minister had arranged that the Banco Nacional of Santo Domingo should get government contracts and that he, Timothy J., was down in Santo Domingo to manage the construction work and see that Minister Sullivan 'got his bit.' Mr. Bryan, the witness said, asked him to write it out and then said, 'Perhaps you don't care to do this?' Bryne said he would be glad to, and the secretary replied that it would not be necessary. 'I got the impression,' said the witness, 'that the secretary did not want the matter on the records of the state department.' New York, Jan. 18.
records.summary_es: The Pierre Weekly Free Press publica: James L. Bryne de Boston, un ingeniero de construcción, declaró que había dicho al Sr. Bryan que el primo del ministro, Timothy J. Sullivan, le había dicho que el ministro había arreglado que el Banco Nacional de Santo Domingo obtuviera contratos del gobierno y que él, Timothy J., estaba en Santo Domingo para dirigir el trabajo de construcción y ver que el ministro Sullivan «recibiera su parte». El testimonio de que el secretario de Estado Bryan fue informado de que James M. Sullivan, ministro americano en la República Dominicana, figuraba en una supuesta conspiración para explotar contratos públicos en esa república, se oyó hoy en la investigación del senador electo Phelan sobre la aptitud del ministro. El Sr. Bryan, dijo el testigo, le pidió que lo escribiera y luego dijo: «Quizás no quieras hacer esto». Bryne dijo que con gusto lo haría, y el secretario respondió que no sería necesario. «Tuve la impresión», dijo el testigo, «de que el secretario no quería que el asunto quedara en los registros del Departamento de Estado». Nueva York, 18 de enero.

records.headline: Sullivan Asked for Graft. W. Lee Sisson Makes Bold Statement Against Dominican Minister.
records.summary_en: The Review prints: New York. W. Lee Sisson, a construction engineer, who said the late Samuel L. Jarvis, controlling the Banco Nacional of Santo Domingo, had asked him to become president of the construction company, testified that F. J. R. Mitchell, president of the bank, had said to him: 'We'll have to take the minister in with us and I think it advisable to do so, as he can be of considerable service in the way of throwing contracts to us.' The witness said he had objected and that Mitchell had replied: 'Well, the minister insists on it,' and he, Mitchell, suggested that 'we might give him a five or ten per cent interest in the company.' James M. Sullivan, minister to the Dominican republic, whose conduct is under investigation here before Senator-elect Phelan of California, was represented by witnesses as having insisted in sharing profits of a construction company organized to obtain work contracts from the Dominican government.
records.summary_es: The Review publica: W. Lee Sisson declaró que F. J. R. Mitchell, presidente del banco, le había dicho: «Tendremos que llevar al ministro con nosotros y creo aconsejable hacerlo, pues puede sernos de considerable servicio en cuanto a conseguirnos contratos». El testigo dijo que había objetado y que Mitchell había respondido: «Bueno, el ministro insiste en ello», y él, Mitchell, sugirió que «podríamos darle un interés del cinco o diez por ciento en la compañía». Sisson, un ingeniero de construcción, dijo que el difunto Samuel L. Jarvis, que controlaba el Banco Nacional de Santo Domingo, le había pedido que fuera presidente de la compañía constructora. James M. Sullivan, ministro en la República Dominicana, cuya conducta se investiga aquí ante el senador electo Phelan de California, fue representado por testigos como quien había insistido en compartir las ganancias de una compañía constructora organizada para obtener contratos de trabajo del gobierno dominicano. Nueva York.

records.headline: The Sentinel=Record prints an item: Minister Sullivan was charged
records.summary_en: The Sentinel=Record prints an item: Minister Sullivan was charged by G. O. Baker, a construction engineer, with taking no steps to protect his property when the city, in possession of revolutionists, was threatened with bombardment by a Dominican gunboat. Baker said he had a contract to build a power plant in Puerto Plata. He said he formally protested to Minister Sullivan and that Sullivan replied: 'Not only will the United States government not prevent the bombardment, but will encourage it.' A letter written by Sullivan to this effect was put into evidence. A copy of it, he said, had been sent to Secretary Bryan. Baker declared Sullivan generally was held responsible for the revolution and charged with precipitating it through his activity with the lease of a railroad to the government, the terms of which the revolutionists objected to. He said Sullivan had once threatened to get him arrested by the Dominicans and had said to him, 'Don't forget that you're not on American soil.' As evidence of conditions in Santo Domingo, Baker said that on one occasion when all Americans 'had taken to the cellar,' it was reported that Desiderio Arias, revolutionist leader, had recommended that 'it would be a good thing to shoot off three or four good Americans' in order to bring about American intervention.
records.summary_es: The Sentinel=Record publica: El ministro Sullivan fue acusado por G. O. Baker, un ingeniero de construcción, de no tomar ninguna medida para proteger su propiedad cuando la ciudad, en posesión de los revolucionarios, estaba amenazada de bombardeo por una cañonera dominicana. Baker dijo que tenía un contrato para construir una planta eléctrica en Puerto Plata. Dijo que protestó formalmente ante el ministro Sullivan y que Sullivan respondió: «El gobierno de los Estados Unidos no solo no impedirá el bombardeo, sino que lo alentará». Una carta escrita por Sullivan en ese sentido fue presentada como evidencia. Una copia de ella, dijo, había sido enviada al secretario Bryan. Baker declaró que Sullivan generalmente era considerado responsable de la revolución y acusado de precipitarla mediante su actividad con el arrendamiento de un ferrocarril al gobierno, cuyos términos objetaban los revolucionarios. Dijo que Sullivan una vez amenazó con hacer que los dominicanos lo arrestaran y le había dicho: «No olvide que no está en suelo americano». Como evidencia de las condiciones en Santo Domingo, Baker dijo que en una ocasión en que todos los americanos «se habían refugiado en el sótano», se informó que Desiderio Arias, líder revolucionario, había recomendado que «sería bueno matar a tiros a tres o cuatro buenos americanos» para provocar la intervención americana.

records.summary_en: The Tabor Independent prints an item: Testimony that Secretary of State Bryan was informed that James M. Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican republic, figured in an alleged conspiracy to exploit public contracts in that republic, was heard today at the inquiry by Senator-elect Phelan into the minister's fitness. James L. Bryne, of Boston, a construction engineer, testified that he had told Mr. Bryan that the minister's cousin, Timothy J. Sullivan, had told him that the minister had arranged that the Banco Nacional of Santo Domingo should get government contracts and that he, Timothy J., was down in Santo Domingo to manage the construction work and see that Minister Sullivan 'got his bit.' Mr. Bryan, the witness said, asked him to write it out and then said, 'Perhaps you don't care to do this?' Bryne said he would be glad to and the secretary replied that it would not be necessary. 'I got the impression,' said the witness, 'that the secretary did not want the matter on the records of the state department.' New York, Jan. 18.
records.summary_es: The Tabor Independent publica una nota: James L. Bryne de Boston, un ingeniero de construcción, declaró que había dicho al Sr. Bryan que el primo del ministro, Timothy J. Sullivan, le había dicho que el ministro había arreglado que el Banco Nacional de Santo Domingo obtuviera contratos del gobierno y que él, Timothy J., estaba en Santo Domingo para dirigir el trabajo de construcción y ver que el ministro Sullivan «recibiera su parte». El testimonio de que el secretario de Estado Bryan fue informado de que James M. Sullivan, ministro americano en la República Dominicana, figuraba en una supuesta conspiración para explotar contratos públicos en esa república, se oyó hoy en la investigación del senador electo Phelan sobre la aptitud del ministro. El Sr. Bryan, dijo el testigo, le pidió que lo escribiera y luego dijo: «Quizás no quieras hacer esto». Bryne dijo que con gusto lo haría, y el secretario respondió que no sería necesario. «Tuve la impresión», dijo el testigo, «de que el secretario no quería que el asunto quedara en los registros del Departamento de Estado». Nueva York, 18 de enero.

records.headline: The Pensacola Journal prints an item: Beer was quoted today
records.summary_en: The Pensacola Journal prints an item: Beer was quoted today at the inquiry into the fitness of James M. Sullivan, the American minister to that republic, as having said he expected to share the profits made in the alleged exploitation with Secretary of State Bryan, former Governor Glynn of New York and Congressman Hamill of New Jersey. M. E. Davis, a New York contractor, testified he had been so informed by Beer. He added that he had taken the statement seriously, but when Senator-elect Phelan, of California, conducting the inquiry, expressed surprise that Davis so regarded it, Davis asserted he now believed the statement to be 'silly rot.' That Sullivan encouraged the Dominican government to bombard the city of Puerto Plata during the revolution in October, 1913, in spite of the fact it would endanger American property there, was charged in the testimony of G. O. Baker, a construction engineer. Baker had a contract to build a power house there. A gunboat subsequently did bombard the city. Albany, N. Y., Jan. 20. 'The statement of M. E. Davis in the investigation of the American minister at San Domingo, that I was interested in the country's matters is an absolute falsehood,' said Former Governor Glynn in a statement tonight. He added he did not know Davis or Sullivan, but was acquainted with W. G. Beer. He declared, however, he was not interested in any enterprise.
records.summary_es: The Pensacola Journal publica una nota: Beer fue citado hoy en la investigación sobre la aptitud de James M. Sullivan, el ministro americano en esa república, como quien había dicho que esperaba compartir las ganancias hechas en la supuesta explotación con el secretario de Estado Bryan, el exgobernador Glynn de Nueva York y el congresista Hamill de Nueva Jersey. M. E. Davis, un contratista de Nueva York, declaró que había sido informado así por Beer. Añadió que había tomado la declaración en serio, pero cuando el senador electo Phelan, de California, que conduce la investigación, expresó sorpresa de que Davis la considerara así, Davis afirmó que ahora creía que la declaración era una «tontería absurda». Que Sullivan alentó al gobierno dominicano a bombardear la ciudad de Puerto Plata durante la revolución en octubre de 1913, a pesar de que ello pondría en peligro la propiedad americana allí, fue denunciado en el testimonio de G. O. Baker, un ingeniero de construcción. Baker tenía un contrato para construir una planta eléctrica allí. Una cañonera bombardeó posteriormente la ciudad. Albany, N. Y., 20 de enero. «La declaración de M. E. Davis en la investigación del ministro americano en San Domingo, de que yo estaba interesado en los asuntos del país es una falsedad absoluta», dijo el exgobernador Glynn en una declaración esta noche. Añadió que no conocía a Davis ni a Sullivan, pero que conocía a W. G. Beer. Declaró, sin embargo, que no estaba interesado en ninguna empresa.

records.headline: The Pensacola Journal prints an item: John G. Gray, of Wilmington
records.summary_en: The Pensacola Journal prints an item: John G. Gray, of Wilmington, Delaware, said that Sullivan was 'actuated by high purposes.' James K. McGuire, former mayor of Syracuse, New York, said Sullivan was 'good enough for San Domingo.' Opponents of Sullivan charge the misuse of his position in connection with the proposed public works contracts in the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: The Pensacola Journal publica una nota: John G. Gray, de Wilmington, Delaware, dijo que Sullivan estaba «movido por altos propósitos». James K. McGuire, exalcalde de Syracuse, Nueva York, dijo que Sullivan era «suficientemente bueno para San Domingo». Los oponentes de Sullivan lo acusan de mal uso de su posición en relación con los propuestos contratos de obras públicas en la República Dominicana.

records.headline: The Evening Journal prints a dispatch: John G. Gray, of Wilmington
records.summary_en: The Evening Journal prints a dispatch: John G. Gray, of Wilmington, a close friend of Secretary Bryan, J. Franklin Fort, former governor of New Jersey, and James K. McGuire, former mayor of Syracuse, were the witnesses who favored Minister Sullivan. Almost the first testimony in favor of James M. Sullivan, minister to Santo Domingo, came in yesterday's hearing before Senator-elect James D. Phelan, President Wilson's commissioner, in the inquiry into the alleged conspiracy to exploit the Dominican republic. New York, Jan. 22. Mr. Gray admitted that he had worked hard to have Sullivan appointed, and said Bryan had been many times a guest at his home in Wilmington. Mr. Gray became incensed at questions by Mr. Strong, the senator-elect's counsel. He objected to what he called a 'political twist' that was given the hearings. 'I don't know why that thing is brought into this inquiry,' stormed Mr. Gray. 'It doesn't belong here. There is some motive behind this investigation that is dragging all this in, and I resent it. It is drawing down this whole inquiry into a field where it doesn't belong. They said I had business interests in San Salvador. That was a fabrication.' He refused to say whether Minor C. Keith was his client or whether Mr. Keith was interested in San Salvador.
records.summary_es: The Evening Journal publica un despacho: John G. Gray, de Wilmington, amigo cercano del secretario Bryan, J. Franklin Fort, exgobernador de Nueva Jersey, y James K. McGuire, exalcalde de Syracuse, fueron los testigos que favorecieron al ministro Sullivan. Casi el primer testimonio a favor de James M. Sullivan, ministro en Santo Domingo, se presentó en la audiencia de ayer ante el senador electo James D. Phelan, comisionado del presidente Wilson, en la investigación sobre la supuesta conspiración para explotar la República Dominicana. Nueva York, 22 de enero. El Sr. Gray admitió que había trabajado duro para que Sullivan fuera nombrado, y dijo que Bryan había sido muchas veces huésped en su casa de Wilmington. El Sr. Gray se indignó con las preguntas del Sr. Strong, abogado del senador electo. Objetó lo que llamó un «giro político» que se daba a las audiencias. «No sé por qué se trae eso a esta investigación», exclamó indignado el Sr. Gray. «Esto no pertenece aquí. Hay algún motivo detrás de esta investigación que arrastra todo esto, y me ofende. Está llevando toda esta investigación a un terreno al que no pertenece. Dijeron que yo tenía intereses comerciales en San Salvador. Eso fue una fabricación». Se negó a decir si Minor C. Keith era su cliente o si el Sr. Keith estaba interesado en San Salvador.

records.headline: The Democratic Banner prints an item: M. E. Davis of New York
records.summary_en: The Democratic Banner prints an item: M. E. Davis of New York, a contractor for supplies, testified he had been informed by Beer while the two were on their way to Santo Domingo, Davis going with the expectation of securing government contracts, which he said Beer had represented to him were to be had. The witness said that at the time he had taken Beer's statement seriously, but now believed the statement to be 'silly rot.' He declared Beer evidently was trying to make an impression and 'using all means in his power to get money.' That Minister Sullivan had encouraged the Dominican government to bombard the city of Puerto Plata during the revolution in October, 1913, in spite of the fact that it would endanger American property there, was charged in testimony by G. O. Baker, a construction engineer. Baker declared Sullivan was generally held responsible for the revolution, and charged with precipitating it through his activity in connection with the lease of a railroad to the government, the terms of which the revolutionists objected to.
records.summary_es: The Democratic Banner publica una nota: M. E. Davis declaró que había sido informado por Beer mientras los dos iban en camino a Santo Domingo, Davis yendo con la expectativa de conseguir contratos del gobierno, que dijo Beer le había representado que podían obtenerse. El testigo, de Nueva York, un contratista de suministros, dijo que en ese momento había tomado en serio la declaración de Beer, pero que ahora creía que la declaración era una «tontería absurda». Declaró que Beer evidentemente trataba de causar una impresión y de «usar todos los medios en su poder para conseguir dinero». Que el ministro Sullivan había alentado al gobierno dominicano a bombardear la ciudad de Puerto Plata durante la revolución en octubre de 1913, a pesar de que ello pondría en peligro la propiedad americana allí, fue denunciado en el testimonio de G. O. Baker, un ingeniero de construcción. Baker declaró que Sullivan generalmente era considerado responsable de la revolución, y acusado de precipitarla mediante su actividad en relación con el arrendamiento de un ferrocarril al gobierno, cuyos términos objetaban los revolucionarios.

records.headline: The Milwaukee Leader prints: Defalcations in the public works
records.summary_en: The Milwaukee Leader prints: Defalcations in the public works department, which may amount to thousands of dollars, were reported here today. The funds are expended under the supervision of the United States government as trustee for the Dominican republic. Details are lacking. Santo Domingo, Jan. 23.
records.summary_es: The Milwaukee Leader publica: Santo Domingo, 23 de enero. Se informaron desfalcos en el departamento de obras públicas, que pueden ascender a miles de dólares. Los fondos se gastan bajo la supervisión del gobierno de los Estados Unidos como fiduciario de la República Dominicana. Faltan detalles.

records.headline: DOMINGO FUNDS MISSING. Sensation Follows Discovery That Thousands Disappeared.
records.summary_en: The Perth Amboy Evening News prints: Santo Domingo, Jan. 23. A sensation has been caused here by the discovery of defalcations in the funds of the public works department amounting to many thousand dollars. The public works funds of the Dominican republic are expended under the supervision of the United States government in its capacity as trustee for the Dominican republic.
records.summary_es: The Perth Amboy Evening News publica: Santo Domingo, 23 de enero. Una sensación ha sido causada aquí por el descubrimiento de desfalcos en los fondos del departamento de obras públicas que ascienden a muchos miles de dólares. Los fondos de obras públicas de la República Dominicana se gastan bajo la supervisión del gobierno de los Estados Unidos en su capacidad de fiduciario de la República Dominicana.

records.headline: The Richmond Times-Dispatch prints an item: Jack Rose, gambler
records.summary_en: The Richmond Times-Dispatch prints an item: Jack Rose, gambler and star witness at Police Lieutenant Charles Becker's trial for the murder of Herman Rosenthal, appeared as a witness for James M. Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican Republic, whose fitness to hold office is under investigation. Rose said he had been lecturing young men to live right, and gave Sullivan credit for inducing him to confess all he knew about the Rosenthal murder, and to become the State's witness. Sullivan at that time was his attorney. Rose declared Sullivan had been 'besieged with threats and promises' because of his activity in obtaining the confession, and suggested that 'the present attack' on the minister might be an aftermath of it. Two letters from Sullivan to James K. McGuire were put in evidence, in which Sullivan said that to earn money to go to law school he had, with the brother of the then Mayor of Waterbury, conducted one boxing match in that city. New York, Jan. 23.
records.summary_es: The Richmond Times-Dispatch publica una nota: Jack Rose, jugador y testigo estrella en el juicio del teniente de policía Charles Becker por el asesinato de Herman Rosenthal, compareció como testigo a favor de James M. Sullivan, ministro americano en la República Dominicana, cuya aptitud para ocupar el cargo está bajo investigación. Rose dijo que había estado dando conferencias a jóvenes sobre vivir rectamente, y dio a Sullivan el crédito de haberlo inducido a confesar todo lo que sabía sobre el asesinato de Rosenthal, y a convertirse en testigo del Estado. Sullivan en ese tiempo era su abogado. Rose declaró que Sullivan había sido «asediado con amenazas y promesas» por su actividad en obtener la confesión, y sugirió que «el presente ataque» contra el ministro podría ser una consecuencia de ello. Dos cartas de Sullivan a James K. McGuire fueron presentadas como evidencia, en las que Sullivan decía que para ganar dinero para ir a la escuela de derecho había, con el hermano del entonces alcalde de Waterbury, realizado un combate de boxeo en esa ciudad. Nueva York, 23 de enero.

records.headline: The Daily Telegram prints an item: M. H. Davis, of New York
records.summary_en: The Daily Telegram prints an item: M. H. Davis, of New York, a contractor for supplies, testified he had been so informed by Beer while the two were on their way to Santo Domingo, Davis with the expectation of securing government contracts, which he said Beer had represented to him were to be had. That Minister Sullivan had encouraged the Dominican government to bombard the city of Puerto Plata during a revolution in October, 1913, in spite of the fact that it would endanger American property there, was charged in the testimony of E. O. Baker, a construction engineer. Baker had a contract for building a power house in that city for a Boston concern and said he protested to Minister Sullivan, asking intervention against a threatened attack upon the city by a Dominican gunboat patrolling the river. The city was at that time in the possession of the revolutionists, and although it was defended by a so-called fort, Baker said it was in no sense fortified, as the entire artillery of the fort consisted of one one-pounder gun. Sullivan, he said, had insisted that it was a fort and that the gunboat had a right to bombard. Baker said he then entered a protest in writing to the minister. To this Sullivan replied in a letter that was put in evidence, in which occurred the sentence: 'This does not mean that the attack on the town will be stopped by the United States; on the contrary we will encourage it.'
records.summary_es: The Daily Telegram publica una nota: M. H. Davis, de Nueva York, un contratista de suministros, declaró que había sido informado así por Beer mientras los dos iban en camino a Santo Domingo, Davis con la expectativa de conseguir contratos del gobierno, que dijo Beer le había representado que podían obtenerse. Que el ministro Sullivan había alentado al gobierno dominicano a bombardear la ciudad de Puerto Plata durante una revolución en octubre de 1913, a pesar de que ello pondría en peligro la propiedad americana allí, fue denunciado en el testimonio de E. O. Baker, un ingeniero de construcción. Baker tenía un contrato para construir una planta eléctrica en esa ciudad para una empresa de Boston y dijo que protestó ante el ministro Sullivan, pidiendo intervención contra un amenazado ataque a la ciudad por una cañonera dominicana que patrullaba el río. La ciudad estaba en ese momento en posesión de los revolucionarios, y aunque estaba defendida por un llamado fuerte, Baker dijo que no estaba fortificada en ningún sentido, ya que toda la artillería del fuerte consistía en un cañón de una libra. Sullivan, dijo, había insistido en que aquello era un fuerte y en que la cañonera tenía derecho a bombardear. Baker dijo que entonces presentó una protesta por escrito al ministro. A esto Sullivan respondió en una carta que fue presentada como evidencia, en la que aparecía la frase: «Esto no significa que el ataque a la ciudad sería detenido por los Estados Unidos; al contrario, lo alentaremos».

records.headline: DEFALCATION NEW SENSATION IN SAN DOMINICAN PROBE Large Sum Said to Be Missing From Funds of Department Under United States Supervision.
records.summary_en: The Evening Public Ledger prints a dispatch reporting misappropriations in the funds of the Department of Public Works amounting to many thousands of dollars. 'The public works funds of the Dominican Republic are expended under the supervision of the United States Government in its capacity as trustee for the Dominican Republic. American officials are said to be involved in the misappropriations, but no detailed information is obtainable. I am informed from official sources that sufficient evidence has been obtained to begin prosecutions, but that the American Minister, James M. Sullivan, has caused further action in the matter to be postponed. Mr. Sullivan is said to have acted upon instructions from Mr. Bryan, Secretary of State, but it cannot be learned why Washington desired the matter to be kept quiet at this time.' The paper also prints an item under the head 'PRESIDENT KNEW LITTLE OF JAMES M. SULLIVAN': New York, Jan. 23. 'He is the President's friend,' was the way the late Samuel M. Jarvis, the banker, referred to James M. Sullivan, Minister to San Domingo, whose official conduct is being investigated by Special Commissioner James D. Phelan, according to Frank J. R. Mitchell, the principal witness at yesterday's session of the inquiry. Mitchell was made president of the Banco Nacional of the island republic when it was organized by Jarvis.
records.summary_es: The Evening Public Ledger publica un despacho sobre malversaciones en los fondos del Departamento de Obras Públicas que ascienden a muchos miles de dólares. «Los fondos de obras públicas de la República Dominicana se gastan bajo la supervisión del gobierno de los Estados Unidos en su capacidad de fiduciario de la República Dominicana. Se dice que funcionarios americanos están involucrados en las malversaciones, pero no se puede obtener información detallada. Estoy informado por fuentes oficiales de que se ha obtenido evidencia suficiente para comenzar procesos, pero que el ministro americano, James M. Sullivan, ha hecho que se posponga toda acción ulterior en el asunto. Se dice que el Sr. Sullivan actuó por instrucciones del Sr. Bryan, secretario de Estado, pero no se puede saber por qué Washington deseaba que el asunto se mantuviera en silencio en este momento». El periódico también publica una nota bajo el título «PRESIDENT KNEW LITTLE OF JAMES M. SULLIVAN»: Nueva York, 23 de enero. «Él es el amigo del Presidente», fue la manera en que el difunto Samuel M. Jarvis, el banquero, se refirió a James M. Sullivan, ministro en San Domingo, cuya conducta oficial está siendo investigada por el comisionado especial James D. Phelan, según Frank J. R. Mitchell, el testigo principal en la sesión de ayer de la investigación. Mitchell fue hecho presidente del Banco Nacional de la república insular cuando fue organizado por Jarvis.

records.headline: The Sunday Telegram prints a dispatch: Washington, Jan. 23.
records.summary_en: The Sunday Telegram prints a dispatch: Washington, Jan. 23. The reported disappearance of some thousands of dollars of public works funds in Santo Domingo occurred before any of the happenings which led up to the present investigation in New York of James M. Sullivan, American minister to Santo Domingo, according to Secretary Bryan's understanding of the situation. He said today he probably would have a statement to make later in regard to the matter and did not care to discuss it until he could present all the facts in the case. It became known today that Enrique Jimenez, nephew of the new president of the Dominican republic and who recently arrived here as minister, had discussed the alleged shortage with State Department officials. It was understood, however, that the amount which is charged as having been taken from the public fund approximated $8,000.
records.summary_es: The Sunday Telegram publica un despacho: Washington, 23 de enero. La desaparición reportada de algunos miles de dólares de fondos de obras públicas en Santo Domingo ocurrió antes que cualquiera de los sucesos que condujeron a la presente investigación en Nueva York de James M. Sullivan, ministro americano en Santo Domingo, según el entendimiento de la situación del secretario Bryan. Dijo hoy que probablemente haría una declaración más tarde con respecto al asunto y que no deseaba discutirlo hasta que pudiera presentar todos los hechos del caso. Se supo hoy que Enrique Jimenez, sobrino del nuevo presidente de la República Dominicana y que recientemente llegó aquí como ministro, había discutido el presunto faltante con funcionarios del Departamento de Estado. Se entendía, sin embargo, que la cantidad que se acusa haber sido tomada del fondo público se aproximaba a $8,000.

records.headline: The Albuquerque Morning Journal prints an item: Enrique Jimenez
records.summary_en: The Albuquerque Morning Journal prints an item: Enrique Jimenez, nephew of the new president of the Dominican republic, who recently arrived here as minister, had discussed the alleged shortage with State Department officials, it became known today. The minister himself denied knowledge of the matter. It was understood, however, that the amount which is charged as having been taken from the public funds approximated $8,000. Secretary Bryan explained that under the situation in operation in Santo Domingo, the American officials who have charge of the collection of customs have nothing to do with the expenditure of that portion of the money which is turned over, with the exception of that which is used for public works.
records.summary_es: The Albuquerque Morning Journal publica una nota: Enrique Jimenez, sobrino del nuevo presidente de la República Dominicana, que recientemente llegó aquí como ministro, había discutido el presunto faltante con funcionarios del Departamento de Estado, se supo hoy. El propio ministro negó conocimiento del asunto. Se entendía, sin embargo, que la cantidad que se acusa haber sido tomada de los fondos públicos se aproximaba a $8,000. El secretario Bryan explicó que bajo la situación en operación en Santo Domingo, los funcionarios americanos que tienen a su cargo la recaudación de aduanas no tienen nada que ver con el gasto de esa porción del dinero que se entrega, con la excepción de la que se usa para obras públicas.

records.headline: The Montgomery Advertiser prints an item: The alleged deficiency
records.summary_en: The Montgomery Advertiser prints an item: The alleged deficiency is about $8,000, and it relates to expenditures made by Dominican officials or Americans appointed by and responsible to the Dominican government over whom the United States government had no direct control. Public works funds of Santo Domingo, reported missing, had disappeared before any of the happenings which led up to the present investigation in New York of James M. Sullivan, American Minister to San Domingo, according to Secretary Bryan's understanding of the situation. He said today he probably would make a statement later in regard to the matter and did not care to discuss it until he could present all the facts. Enrique Jimenez, nephew of the new president of the Dominican Republic, who recently arrived here as minister, has discussed the alleged shortage with State Department officials. The minister himself denied all knowledge of the matter. It was understood the amount missing is approximately $8,000.
records.summary_es: The Montgomery Advertiser publica una nota: La presunta deficiencia es de unos $8,000, y se relaciona con gastos hechos por funcionarios dominicanos o por americanos nombrados por el gobierno dominicano y responsables ante él, sobre quienes el gobierno de los Estados Unidos no tenía control directo. Los fondos de obras públicas de Santo Domingo, reportados como desaparecidos, habían desaparecido antes que cualquiera de los sucesos que condujeron a la presente investigación en Nueva York de James M. Sullivan, ministro americano en San Domingo, según el entendimiento de la situación del secretario Bryan. Dijo hoy que probablemente haría una declaración más tarde con respecto al asunto y que no deseaba discutirlo hasta que pudiera presentar todos los hechos. Enrique Jimenez, sobrino del nuevo presidente de la República Dominicana, que recientemente llegó aquí como ministro, ha discutido el presunto faltante con funcionarios del Departamento de Estado. El propio ministro negó todo conocimiento del asunto. Se entendía que la cantidad desaparecida es de aproximadamente $8,000.

records.headline: The Alleged Dominican Shortage.
records.summary_en: The Evening Star prints an editorial on the report of a deficit in the funds of the Dominican Republic, over which the United States exercises a custodial supervision: The money loss, which would presumably have to be made good by this government, is inconsequential, but the damage to American prestige in the countries of the south and the West Indies would be serious if such a deficit were in fact to have resulted from the carelessness of any official named by the United States. The strictest honesty and the most scrupulous care in safeguarding the financial interests of Santo Domingo are demanded. Especially is it important to maintain a clean slate in this respect, in view of the inquiry now in progress respecting the influences which operated in the selection of representatives of this country in the island republic. The result of the present investigation, directed by the Secretary of State, will be awaited with the keenest interest.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star comenta en un editorial el informe de un déficit en los fondos de la República Dominicana, sobre los cuales los Estados Unidos ejercen una supervisión de custodia: La pérdida de dinero, que presumiblemente tendría que ser repuesta por este gobierno, es de poca importancia, pero el daño al prestigio americano en los países del sur y las Indias Occidentales sería serio si tal déficit hubiera resultado en efecto de la negligencia de cualquier funcionario nombrado por los Estados Unidos. Se demanda la más estricta honestidad y el más escrupuloso cuidado en salvaguardar los intereses financieros de Santo Domingo. Especialmente es importante mantener un historial limpio en este respecto, en vista de la investigación ahora en curso respecto a las influencias que operaron en la selección de representantes de este país en la república insular. El resultado de la presente investigación, dirigida por el secretario de Estado, será esperado con el más vivo interés.

records.headline: The Tulsa Daily World prints an item: Mitchell took the stand
records.summary_en: The Tulsa Daily World prints an item: Mitchell took the stand today at the investigation of the fitness of James M. Sullivan to retain his post as American minister to the Dominican republic. He was asked if he intended to accuse W. W. Russell, Sullivan's predecessor, with dishonesty, when he said in his testimony Friday that had there been an honest American minister at Santo Domingo before Sullivan took the post the Banco Nacional would have received without asking the deposit of customs receipts. Mitchell said he did not mean to imply 'absolute dishonesty,' but that Russell had been unfair to the institution. He said he had based his statement on 'the fact I had been told that Minister Russell had advocated that the Dominican government's loan be given to the National City Bank of New York because it would better suit the Washington government.'
records.summary_es: The Tulsa Daily World publica una nota: Mitchell subió al estrado hoy en la investigación sobre la aptitud de James M. Sullivan para retener su puesto como ministro americano en la República Dominicana. Se le preguntó si intentaba acusar de deshonestidad a W. W. Russell, predecesor de Sullivan, cuando dijo en su testimonio del viernes que si hubiera habido un ministro americano honesto en Santo Domingo antes de que Sullivan tomara el puesto, el Banco Nacional habría recibido sin pedirlo el depósito de las rentas aduaneras. Mitchell dijo que no quiso implicar una «deshonestidad absoluta», sino que Russell había sido injusto con la institución. Dijo que había basado su declaración en «el hecho de que se me había dicho que el ministro Russell había abogado porque el préstamo del gobierno dominicano fuera dado al National City Bank de Nueva York porque convendría mejor al gobierno de Washington».

records.headline: The Norwich Bulletin prints an item: At the investigation of Senator-elect James D. Phelan
records.summary_en: The Norwich Bulletin prints an item: At the investigation of Senator-elect James D. Phelan into the fitness of Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican republic, to hold his post, Collett asserted that in his opinion Sullivan was eminently fit to represent the United States in Santo Domingo in the double capacity in which the American minister there is obliged to act, that of business man as well as diplomat. Collett is a son-in-law of former Mayor Dahlman of Omaha, Neb., and said that his wife's family and Secretary Bryan's were personal friends. He had not been recommended for his post by Secretary Bryan, he said, until after he had passed a civil service examination as engineer for the Interstate Commerce Commission. Sullivan, he conceded, was not popular with Dominicans, but he held that Sullivan was not to blame. 'I don't think any American minister to Santo Domingo ever will be popular,' he asserted. 'Santo Dominicans are always against their government and if this government is recognized by the United States, the American minister is bound to be unpopular. Santo Domingo is a hotbed of criticism anyway. If you don't get criticised down there you are not doing anything.'

records.headline: GRAY TESTIFIES ABOUT SULLIVAN Delaware Man Says He Approached Bryan as Matter of Right UNFAIR IMPUTATION MADE
records.summary_en: The Montgomery Advertiser prints an item: New York, Jan. 27. John G. Gray of Wilmington, Del., who was influential in obtaining the appointment of James M. Sullivan as minister to the Dominican republic, testified today at the investigation into the fitness of the Minister to hold his post. Mr. Gray said he became attorney for the Banco Nacional of Santo Domingo long after Sullivan was appointed. He 'slipped in,' he said, because the Banco Nacional had been placed in an awkward position through inability to secure payment of loans from the Dominican government. He declared he had not gone to Secretary Bryan in the matter to 'obtain a personal favor,' but that it was a matter of legal right. 'I considered it an honorable matter to take up,' he said, adding that advocacy of Sullivan was an entirely separate matter from his subsequently representing the bank. He said 'unfair imputations' had got into the newspapers to the effect that he had originally sought Sullivan's appointment in behalf of the Banco Nacional's interests.

Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican republic, to hold his post, Collett asserted that in his opinion Sullivan was eminently fit to represent the United States in Santo Domingo in the double capacity in which the American minister there is obliged to act, that of business man as well as diplomat. Collett is a son-in-law of former Mayor James C. Dahlman of Omaha, Neb., and said his wife's family and Secretary Bryan's were personal friends. He had not been recommended for his post, he said, until after he had passed a civil service examination as engineer for the Interstate Commerce Commission. Sullivan, he conceded, was not popular with Dominicans, but he held that Sullivan was not to blame. 'I don't think any American minister to Santo Domingo ever will be popular,' he asserted. 'Santo Dominicans are always against their government, and if this government is recognized by the United States the American minister is bound to be unpopular.' Never, said Collett, had he been asked by Sullivan to favor one contractor above another, nor had he seen anything in the minister's private or official conduct that was improper. Commissioner Phelan announced that documents received from Minister Sullivan in his defense would be put into evidence tomorrow and that the investigation would then recess to be resumed in Washington on Monday or Tuesday of next week.

records.headline: The Albuquerque Morning Journal prints an item: James M. Sullivan
records.summary_en: The Albuquerque Morning Journal prints an item: James M. Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican republic, denied all the charges of unfitness made against him, chiefly by Walker W. Vick, former receiver general of customs of Santo Domingo, in a statement read in evidence today at the hearings into the charges before Senator-elect Phelan of California. New York, Jan. 28. The statement, received by mail, was supported by documentary evidence and made counter-charges against Vick. Sullivan declared he had been made the victim of a newspaper campaign engineered by Vick to attack his character and conduct, which was unsupported by facts. He said certain newspapers in the United States had 'championed the cause of as audacious a gang of pirates as ever sailed the Caribbean sea.' Sullivan said he had no apology to make for recommending as the depository for the receivership funds the Banco Nacionale, which Vick charges was an untrustworthy institution and which had been accused of seeking the appointment of Sullivan. 'The records of the State Department will show,' he wrote, 'that I never recommended any one bank above another,' except that he preferred some American bank, stating that if the American banks here were not satisfactory the department should urge some responsible bank in America to open a bank here.

Vick, ex recaudador general de aduanas de Santo Domingo, en una declaración leída como evidencia hoy en las audiencias sobre las acusaciones ante el senador electo Phelan de California. Nueva York, 28 de enero. La declaración, recibida por correo, estaba apoyada por evidencia documental e hizo contraacusaciones contra Vick. Sullivan declaró que había sido hecho víctima de una campaña de prensa orquestada por Vick para atacar su carácter y su conducta, que carecía de apoyo en los hechos. Dijo que ciertos periódicos en los Estados Unidos habían «defendido la causa de una banda de piratas tan audaz como jamás haya navegado el mar Caribe». Sullivan dijo que no tenía disculpa que hacer por recomendar como depositario de los fondos de la receptoría el Banco Nacionale, que Vick acusa era una institución indigna de confianza y que ha sido acusado de buscar el nombramiento de Sullivan. «Los registros del Departamento de Estado mostrarán», escribió, «que nunca recomendé un banco sobre otro», excepto que prefería algún banco americano, declarando que si los bancos americanos aquí no fueran satisfactorios el departamento debería urgir a algún banco responsable en América a abrir un banco aquí.

Sullivan, American minister to that republic, as having said he expected to share what profits he made in the alleged exploitation with Secretary of State Bryan, Martin H. Glynn, former governor of New York, and Congressman James E. Hamill of New Jersey. M. E. Davis of New York, a contractor, testified he had been so informed by Beer. records.headline: SULLIVAN DENIES ALL CHARGES OF UNFITNESS American Minister in Letter Makes Counter Assault on Vick
records.summary_en: The New Britain Herald prints an item: A statement by Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican republic, denying all the charges of unfitness made against him, chiefly by Walker W. Vick, former receiver general of customs of Santo Domingo, was read in evidence yesterday at the hearings into the charges before Senator-elect Phelan. He said that certain newspapers in the United States had 'championed the cause of as audacious a gang of pirates as ever sailed the Caribbean.' Sullivan said he had no apology to make for recommending the Banco Nacional as the depository for the receivership funds, which Vick charges was an untrustworthy institution and which has been accused of seeking the appointment of Sullivan in order to exploit the island. records.headline: PHELAN, AFTER HEARINGS, TO GO TO SANTO DOMINGO Secretary Bryan Says He Is Willing to Make Statement in Sullivan Case if Desired.

Sullivan, American minister to the Dominican Republic, will go to Santo Domingo City at the close of the hearings which he purposes to hold in Washington.
